subject: FinCloud: incident sitrep + evidence onboarding request
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@fincloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fincloud.com, sre-eng@fincloud.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinCloud — unusual request pattern (initial notice)

Hi Diego,

Quick heads-up from our ops team: between 02:18 and 02:35 UTC this morning we observed a spike of 58k API calls coming from multiple IPs associated with a subset of our prod tokens that map to Redwood-backed routes. The pattern looks like high-volume automated requests targeting embedding endpoints (sequence lengths ~4–8), and several requests contained unusual prompt payloads.

We turned throttling on for the affected keys and have preserved logs, but our compliance team asked us to escalate to Redwood for a joint investigation and evidence exchange (SOC2/SIG artifacts requested). Can you confirm whether you see correlated traffic on your side, and share your incident response plan and any immediate artifacts you can provide (audit logs, auth logs, token issuance timestamps)?

We need a short sitrep (what you’ve observed, actions taken, and a list of artifacts you can share) so we can complete an initial evidence packet for our legal/compliance review.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Zhang
Security Operations Lead, FinCloud Technologies
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@fincloud.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinCloud — unusual request pattern (initial notice)

Emily — thanks for the alert and for preserving the logs. We’ve opened Jira SEC-4321 to track the joint investigation. Immediate notes from our side: 

- We see the same anomalous request surge in our edge telemetry between 02:15–02:40 UTC, primarily hitting embedding routes.
- We rate-limited the affected tokens at 09:05 PDT and rotated the problematic keys at 09:10 PDT as a precaution.
- No indications so far of data exfiltration beyond the requests themselves; payloads appear to be non-sensitive strings rather than structured PII. We’re continuing analysis.

Next actions (short timeline):
- Olga will pull correlated auth/API gateway traces and a token issuance timeline (ETA 2 hours).
- Marissa will prepare a minimal forensics bundle (network flow summaries, top 10 client IPs, request hashes) for secure transfer.
- I’ll share our Incident Response Plan v1 and a checklist of artifacts we typically exchange for SOC2/SIG evidence.

Can you confirm the best delivery channel for the evidence bundle (secure S3 presigned link or encrypted Drive)? Also let us know any legal/regulatory constraints (DPA clauses) that affect retention or redaction.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@fincloud.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Action: evidence checklist + IRP share (redwood_irp_v1 attached)

Emily — attaching our IRP snapshot (redwood_irp_v1.pdf) and an evidence checklist to help FinCloud’s compliance team ingest artifacts. We can upload larger bundles to a presigned Drive/S3 link once you confirm.

Evidence checklist (requested artifacts & typical formats):
- Access / auth logs: timestamped auth attempts and token issuance events (CSV or ndjson) — required
- API gateway request logs: request id, client ip, user-agent, endpoint, response code, latency (ndjson) — required
- Network flow summary: top talkers for the 02:00–03:00 UTC window (pcap summary or aggregated csv) — preferred
- KV / prefix cache snapshots (if applicable): list of recent cache keys for the affected tokens — optional, ask before sharing
- Forensics summary: triage notes + root-cause hypothesis (PDF) — helpful
- Signed attestation: who handled evidence transfer + chain-of-custody (PDF) — helpful

Attachments included: redwood_irp_v1.pdf (Redwood incident response plan excerpt), forensics_summary.zip (initial triage notes, hashes), network-logs-20270402.tar.gz (aggregated edge logs).

Security/transfer notes: 
- We prefer a presigned S3 link with AES-256 encryption and a 72-hour expiry for large bundles.
- If FinCloud needs an encrypted container, we can provide a PGP key for the transfer.

Olga/Marissa: please assemble the artifacts per checklist and post to the SEC-4321 ticket when ready. Emily — confirm transfer method and any required redactions; we’ll proceed ASAP.

Quoted message for context:
> On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 09:12 AM Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@fincloud.com> wrote:
> > Quick heads-up from our ops team: between 02:18 and 02:35 UTC this morning we observed a spike of 58k API calls ...

— Diego
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@fincloud.com>, ops@fincloud.com
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: FinCloud — sitrep and evidence handoff (postmortem attached)

Emily / ops team — final update for today and the handoff bundle.

Summary (short):
- Timeline: anomalous traffic 02:15–02:40 UTC; Redwood mitigations (rate-limit, key rotation) completed by 09:10 PDT.
- Impact: transient increase in error rates for a small cohort of FinCloud keys; no confirmed exfil of sensitive records.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): automated scraper using a set of compromised client tokens; ongoing attribution work.

Files delivered via presigned Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/fincloud/20270402-evidence (link expires in 7 days).
Delivered items (attachments): customer_postmortem_fincloud_20270402.pdf (formal timeline & mitigations), forensics_summary.zip (triage notes, request hashes), network-logs-20270402.tar.gz (aggregated edge logs).

Next steps:
- FinCloud compliance: confirm receipt and indicate any redaction needs.
- Joint follow-up: schedule a short call (30 min) tomorrow to review the postmortem and sign chain-of-custody if needed.

Thanks for the fast coordination. I’ll leave SEC-4321 updated with artifacts and notes.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — security@redwood.com
